subject: BrightWave: Quality guardrails & eval integration — CS handoff
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: BrightWave kickoff — quality guardrails & eval handoff

Monica,

Thanks again for the engagement — BrightWave (contact: Nora Liu) signed last week and is ready to move into implementation. I'm handing off the quality/monitoring scope to CS and SE so you can drive the eval-harness integration and define regression alerts. High level summary below; attached is the prompt set we used in the POC and a first-pass eval config.

Summary (POC findings)
- Model: open-llama-15B-quant (prod variant TBD)
- Primary flows: question-answering over KnowledgeBase v2, summarization for long transcripts
- Failure modes observed: hallucination on entity lookups (~6% POC), occasional verbatim leakage for sensitive PII prompts (rare)
- Latency target: p95 < 450ms for short queries (<=256 tokens)
- Cost sensitivity: BrightWave wants to keep per-1000-token cost under their internal threshold

What I attached: BrightWave_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (gold/good/bad examples), bw_eval_config_v1.yaml (initial metrics), demo logs excerpt.

Key asks for CS/SE:
1) Decide the canonical prompt sets to pin for canary (suggest: start with prompt_set_v1 as "canary" and add a smaller set for fast regression checks).
2) Bake eval harness steps into their CI or into Redwood Optimize pipeline: acceptance metrics, thresholds, and automatic regression alerting (notify CS & AE).
3) Define canary rollout policy: start at 10% traffic for 48h, escalate to 50% for 24h, full rollout after no regressions for 72h. Define rollback triggers (see suggested policy below).
4) Confirm who at BrightWave gets access to run ad-hoc evals and who receives alerts.

Suggested rollback triggers (initial):
- Quality: >3% relative increase in hallucination rate vs baseline OR absolute increase of 2 percentage points
- Cost: >25% higher per-token cost than baseline
- Latency: p95 breaches >2x target for two consecutive windows (15m)

Next steps: Can we schedule a CS/SE technical kickoff on Tuesday 2026-05-12? Nora is available in the morning Pacific.

Cheers,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: BrightWave_prompt_set_v1.jsonl; bw_eval_config_v1.yaml

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Nora Liu <nora@brightwave.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightWave kickoff — quality guardrails & eval handoff

Thanks Karthik — looping in the CS and applied-ML owners. Nora, hi — excited to work with you. Quick clarifying q's before the kickoff so we can prep the eval harness and monitoring: 

1) Can you confirm which environments you want us to run the canary in (staging sandbox vs full prod)? We recommend the sandbox for the initial 10% canary but need the sandbox to mirror your KB snapshot.
2) Which metrics are BrightWave most sensitive to? From Karthik's notes we'll prioritize hallucination rate and latency, but if you have precision/recall goals for QA that will change the eval config.
3) Are you able to provide a small set of labeled edge-case examples (10–20) that should never regress? If so, we can include them as breaking tests.

On our side: Marissa will own the eval harness integration with your CI/CD and Evelyn will define the statistical tests and alert thresholds. Proposed agenda for the 45m kickoff: introductions, access & endpoints, prompt set review, eval config walkthrough, canary/rollback policy sign-off, timeline & SOW items.

Can we lock Tuesday 2026-05-12 at 10:00am PT? If that works Nora, please share the sandbox credentials or a short-lived token for our SEs.

Thanks,
Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Nora Liu <nora@brightwave.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 07:58:00 -0700
Subject: RE: BrightWave kickoff — quality guardrails & eval handoff

Hi all — a few technical notes ahead of the call so we can move quickly:

- Eval harness integration: we can push a Jenkins/GitHub Action that runs the bw_eval_config_v1.yaml suite against your staging endpoint. We'll need a stable endpoint and a token with 'eval' scope. If you prefer we can run within Redwood's hosted eval pipeline and share results via Drive and webhook.

- Metrics and tests to include (initial):
  * Hallucination rate (entity hallucinations), measured by exact-match labels in prompt_set_v1; threshold: baseline +2 ppt absolute or 30% relative
  * ROUGE-L / BLEU for summaries (if you use extractive scoring) — baseline thresholds in config
  * Latency: p50/p95; gating at p95 <450ms
  * Safety: PII detection failures (block on any confirmed leakage in the breaking set)

- Canary rollout suggestion: 10% -> 25% -> 100% with automated checks after each stage. I recommend an automatic abort if any breaking test fails or if any metric breaches rollback triggers across two consecutive sampling windows (15m). We can implement the canary using request-weight routing in Redwood Dedicated or via feature-flagging in your proxy.

- Automation & alerts: we'll push to your webhook URL /internal/cs-evals and set up summary emails for the AE and CS with daily digest. We will also create a Jira (CS-1274) for tracking.

I'll attach a starter eval config (bw_eval_config_v1.yaml) with the tests above. I'll also add a condensed checklist for the kickoff.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: bw_eval_config_v1.yaml

Thanks, Monica and Marissa — Tuesday 10:00am PT works. We will provide the staging endpoint and a short-lived token by end of day Monday.

Answers to questions:
- Environment: please run the 10% initial canary against our staging cluster (staging mirrors prod KB snapshot).
- Metrics of highest priority: hallucination rate first, then summarization quality. Latency is important but we can tolerate short spikes during canary if they stabilise.
- Labeled edge cases: attaching 15 human-labeled edge cases now (I put them in the folder linked in the Drive share Karthik mentioned).

Tom (cc'd) is our implementation lead — Tom.Reyes will coordinate scoped access. He will join the kickoff.

Best,
Nora
Director of Product, BrightWave AI

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Nora Liu <nora@brightwave.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: BrightWave — post-kickoff notes & next steps (canary + rollback policy)

Team — short internal summary and action items after confirming the kickoff & assets with BrightWave. Nora provided the sandbox and labeled edge cases in the Drive link.

Action items (owners & ETA)
- Marissa: push eval-harness GH Action and seed it with bw_eval_config_v1.yaml. Make the webhook for alerts. ETA: 2026-05-18 EOD.
- Evelyn: define the statistical test and exact alerting thresholds (will iterate on the 2ppt / 30% guidance). ETA: 2026-05-17 noon.
- Rishi: own the rollout orchestration and incident response playbook (toggle plan, how to rollback, Slack alert templates). ETA: 2026-05-19 COB.
- Karthik: finalize SOW changes for the quality monitoring add-on and send to Nora. I'll attach the SOW to this thread.
- Monica: schedule daily check-ins for the first 72h of canary and set up a shared status doc.

Canary & rollback (finalized draft)
- Phases: 10% (48h) -> 25% (24h) -> 100% (no regressions for 72h)
- Abort/rollback conditions: any breaking test fails OR hallucination rate increases by +2 ppt absolute OR p95 latency >900ms for two consecutive 15m windows OR per-token cost >25% above baseline for 1h.
- Rollback procedure: immediate traffic shift to previous variant, create incident in Jira CS-1274, notify AE/CS via slack #cs-brightwave and email digest.

Attachments: SOW_BrightWave_v2.pdf (please review wording on the monitoring SLA and acceptance criteria — Karthik will lead commercial).

I'll host the kickoff notes and the shared status doc in Drive; will share link once created.

—Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
